A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAR research work. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison; retained sections, equations, tables, and figures can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and UCF-101 generation results, design ablations in Tables 2–4, and conditional-entropy experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds optimized inference measurements in Table 7 and generation examples in Figures 6–7.

M1.justification: PAR retains the same cross-region grouping, sequential initialization, learnable transition tokens, grouped attention, and model architectures. The additional compilation experiments do not revise the proposed generation algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds a zero-shot resolution-extrapolation scenario: generation at 512×512 after training at 384×384. The ImageNet and UCF-101 benchmark coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds vLLM-optimized LlamaGen-3B as an explicitly evaluated comparison variant. The comparator sets in the original image and video comparisons in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces a latency comparison using PyTorch compile for PAR and vLLM for LlamaGen, with 384×384 generation, batch size 1, and one A100 GPU. The existing training budgets and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an engineering-optimization compatibility study and qualitative checks of resolution extrapolation and long-range visual consistency. The original design ablations and conditional-entropy analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The added latency table continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds latencies of 4.12s for LlamaGen-3B with vLLM, 1.15s for compiled PAR-3B-4×, and 0.43s for compiled PAR-3B-16×. These are results under added optimization settings. Figures 6–7 add qualitative outcomes; the original benchmark scores, ablation values, and entropy plots are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and Algorithm 1's conditional-entropy estimator are unchanged. The entropy derivation and analysis move from Appendix C to Appendix D rather than constituting new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dependency-based parallel-generation contribution and headline claims of 3.6× speedup with comparable quality and up to 9.5× with minimal degradation. The appendix additions provide support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 argues that PAR and engineering optimizations provide complementary benefits, explains resolution extrapolation through rotary positional embeddings, and discusses consistency despite strong dependencies between distant features. These extend the interpretation of applicability beyond v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added execution backends, updates the project-page address, and attributes the video-tokenizer reproduction to Next Block Prediction in Section 4.1. The tokenizer attribution change alone does not establish a different tokenizer configuration; Tables 5–6 retain their hyperparameters.

R1.justification: Four references are added: the Next Token Prediction survey, RandAR, Next Block Prediction, and the vLLM/PagedAttention work. These update contextual citations and implementation attribution without substantially revising the related-work narrative.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and affiliation edits, adds acknowledgements, and expands the appendix roadmap with an optimization section and visualization subheadings. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7 and Figures 6–7. Previous supplementary Figures 6–10 are retained as Figures 8–12, with appendix reflow and limited caption-formatting changes rather than a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 7 strengthens the practical efficiency evidence by comparing against an optimized LlamaGen implementation and demonstrating compatibility with compilation. The new resolution and consistency examples modestly broaden empirical support. These gains are limited: the original benchmarks remain unchanged, and the additional generalization checks are qualitative.
